description: Scale Session triage call script (Mariana-led qualification call before the closer's strategy call with John). Each stage has the verbatim script, a clear goal, green-light criteria the rep must hit before moving on, uncertainty triggers, and the exact pushback script.

stages.name: 1. Opening
stages.tone: Sit back, relax, speak slowly and calmly.
stages.goal: Make sure you know WHY they booked the call. NO PAIN = NO MORE TALKING. Don't move on until you know.
say: Hi [name]. Tell me about your day. (If they're busy: 'Oh [name], is now no longer a good time?')
Fantastic over here!

I'm Mariana, I oversee and direct the entire social media and content strategy for Lauren's brand. (For context: I've closed multiple 7 figures in cash for Lauren and I've been with her over the last half decade.)
I have a note in my calendar that you're interested in generating more revenue from your social media.
So over the next 10-15 minutes of this call, in an ideal world, what are you most hoping to get out of our conversation together?
(Let them reply.)

Ok awesome. From our 7 years in this business, we know that alignment is important to a healthy relationship. So this call may feel pretty basic but that doesn't mean it isn't important because we'll go through a few specifics, to see if we can help. Ok?
If we can help you, I'll let you know, and we'll arrange a second call to go through things in more detail. And if not, I'll aim to point you in the right direction. Is that ok [name]?
Ok great. So you know we're all about driving revenue from social media. That's what inspired you to want to speak with us, right?
(If they don't elaborate on WHY they booked: 'Ok gotcha. So that I can understand your situation, what made you want to decide to book this call with us? What problem are you hoping we can solve?')
green_light: You know the specific reason they booked the call
There is a clear pain or goal they want help with
stages.pushback_script:
IDK what you guys do — How did you end up on this call then? Ok cool no worries then, in an ideal world what would you like to get out of this call?

If they say 'just to learn more about ___': 'Got it, and I can imagine you're quite busy right?' (PAUSE — let them say yes.) Then half laughing with a smile: 'Yeah. And just so we can see what could best help… Do you go around jumping on calls to learn more all day? Or are you here because you're interested in potentially working with us, if you think it could help?'

stages.name: 2. ICP Check
stages.tone: Confident — you've already done your homework on their socials.
stages.goal: Confirm they're in our ideal client profile. If obviously ICP from their socials (good audience, real business), don't dive deep here.
say: (Check their socials BEFORE the call. If they're obviously ICP, don't dive deep — just say:)

So first of all, great work building such a big audience. I saw you have [X] followers on [PLATFORM]. Is that where you drive most of your revenue from? Or is there another platform like email or ads where you're bringing in most of your new clients?
So I did check your [platform] and noticed [problem — e.g. low engagement, big audience but very few comments].
(And I know you had a brief conversation with Lauren.)
Is that the main place you're getting your new clients from? Or do you use something else like YouTube, email, ads, LinkedIn?
green_light: You know which platform drives their revenue
You've named the specific gap you noticed on their socials
stages.pushback_script: Don't accept 'a bit of everything' here. Pin it down: 'Got it — but if you had to point to the ONE platform that's bringing in the most revenue right now, which one would it be?' You need a clear answer so the closer knows where they're at.

stages.name: 3. Results & Goal
stages.tone: Visionary — paint the picture.
stages.goal: Clarity that their goal is a good goal and realistic for us to hit (e.g. add a lot of revenue — more than 10k per month additionally — or get speaking gigs from organic). DO NOT MOVE ON until you are certain they have a goal we can help with.
say: Ok, so let's jump 3 years into the future. Lauren, you and I are at your favourite dinner spot, eating your favourite meal, looking back on the last 3 years celebrating our successful collaboration. What are the top 2 or 3 wins we're celebrating together?

Love it, that's worth celebrating over. And because we're all about driving revenue with social media, just like a personal trainer would need to know your ideal body shape and fitness goals so we have a target, where exactly would you like to get to revenue wise in 1 year from now, and 3 years from now?
Cool — that's clear. Thank you. So that I can understand your business better, if that's where you want to be… how far off are you right now from that monthly revenue level?
green_light: They've named a specific monthly revenue target
The target is realistic + something we can help with (≥ +10k/mo or speaking gigs from organic)
You know the gap between current and goal
stages.pushback_script: This goal isn't clear enough. You can't pass them to the closer with vague goals. Push: 'I hear you — but to make sure we're not wasting your time, I need a specific number. If you could click your fingers and have anything, what's the monthly revenue you'd want to be at in 12 months? Just throw a number at me — there's no wrong answer.' Do not move on until you have a number.

stages.name: 4. Current Revenue
stages.tone: Curious + non-judgemental.
stages.goal: Get clear on their current monthly revenue. Doesn't matter what it is — but important we know so the closer can pitch the right level of support.
say: Ok got it, so your monthly revenue over the last 6 months, what has it been exactly? I ask so that I can see which of our levels of support might make the most sense for you.
green_light: You have a specific monthly revenue figure (or a clear range)
stages.pushback_script: Don't accept vague here. The closer needs a real number. Push gently: 'Totally get it varies — but over the last 6 months on average, what would you say it's been per month? Doesn't have to be exact, just a real ballpark so I can match you to the right level of support.' Hold for the answer.

stages.name: 5. Past Attempts
stages.tone: Curious — chase what they liked/disliked.
stages.goal: List down how they want to get support and pass it to the closer. Doesn't matter what they say but it's important we know.
say: Have you worked with anyone else or any other companies to help with this before?
(Let them reply.)
What did you like or dislike about it?
Thank you for sharing. What attracted you to the Scale Systems way of doing things? What did you like about our method specifically?
(IF they say they have a coach OR are working with someone else now:)
Got you, seeing as you're already working with someone else — what's not working as well as it should be that means you're interested in working with us?
green_light: You know if they've worked with similar companies before
You know what attracted them to Scale Systems specifically
If they have a current coach: you know what's not working
stages.pushback_script: If they can't articulate what attracted them to us, that's a soft answer. Push: 'Got it — but specifically, was it the AI content angle, the revenue focus, something Lauren said? Just so I know what most resonated with you.' This helps the closer hit the right angle.

stages.name: 6. Time & Urgency
stages.tone: Direct — you're qualifying their commitment.
stages.goal: Get clear they have ~1 hour per day and they want help NOW. If they don't, note it for the closer but pass them through anyway — the closer can overcome it.
say: Got it. So how much time do you have to focus on driving revenue into your business per day?
Right and how soon are you looking to get help with this?

The reason I ask is that we have a couple of specific offers on right now, so I just want to ensure the timing is good for you to get support from us if we can help. Would there be any obstacles that would prevent you from moving forwards if we felt like it was a fit?
green_light: You know they have at least 1 hour per day
They've said they want help now (not 'someday')
You know any obstacles upfront
stages.pushback_script: Stalling on urgency. Push with the qualifier: 'Got it, and if you were certain this would add decent revenue to your business on a monthly basis, would that change things?' (ONLY use this if they aren't financially qualified or are giving a BS answer.) Even if they're still stalling, pass them through to the closer — closer can overcome this. But make sure the closer knows they aren't rushing to move forward now, so the closer can prepare.

stages.name: 7. Budget
stages.tone: Anchored + confident. You're not negotiating — you're stating the range.
stages.goal: Get a real number from them OR confirm the 2k-6k/month range works. If they give a low number you think they could stretch, run the stretch question.
say: Got it. So your goal of [X] is clear, and I understand you're interested in working with us because of [pain].
So how much have you set aside to invest in getting this working.
Most people in your position typically invest between **2k to 6k a month** to see results like you're looking for. Does that align with what you're prepared for?
STRETCH (if they give a low number but you feel they could do more): 'And if you knew that this would allow you to [insert problems they have], would you be able to stretch that?'
IF THEY SAY 'I could do that on a payment plan': Get the exact amount they could do. 'Cool, so 1-6k per month wouldn't be an issue for you if you were sure it'd work?'
green_light: They've confirmed 2k-6k/month aligns OR
They've given a specific real number you can pass to the closer
pushback_triggers: i don't really have a budget
stages.pushback_script:
Hhhhmmm okay OR Got it — and so we can see which of our options could be feasible, on a monthly basis, what are you willing to invest to be sure you'd get this working?

If they STILL won't give a number — push once more: 'Just throw out a real number, even if it's a rough one. There's no wrong answer — it just helps me match you to the right tier.' Don't move on without a number you can pass to the closer.

stages.name: 8. Authority
stages.tone: Half laughing on the close — light but pinning it down.
stages.goal: Surface every decision-maker now so the closer doesn't get blindsided by a spouse / accountant / business partner objection.
say: Ok thank you. So for your social media, do you have someone on your team who helps with any of this? Like a VA or an appointment setter or something?
And is there anyone else involved in making decisions when it comes to your business or is that something you have full autonomy over?
(If they say 'just me' — say this half laughing:)
Ok got it, so you're not going to hit us with an objection like 'I need to speak to my partner?' or 'I have to run this by my accountant?' right?
green_light: You know who else is in the decision (spouse, partner, accountant, team)
OR you've pinned down it's just them and they've confirmed no surprise stakeholders
stages.pushback_script: They just surfaced a hidden decision-maker. Pin it down NOW so the closer isn't ambushed: 'Got it — who specifically, and what would they need to be comfortable with for this to be a yes?' Note it for the closer. A hidden stakeholder kills the close.

stages.name: 9a. Fit — Pass to Closer
stages.tone: [SLOW + CONFIDENT TONALITY]
stages.goal: Book the strategy call with John (closer) and hold them accountable to watching the pre-call doc.
say: Cool. So with what you're looking to do, it's a pretty straightforward problem for us to solve.

Now I am going to get you to have a 1:1 interview with Lauren's business partner directly, John, to go through the details and specifics on how it'll work for you, to ensure you [overcome the problem they have].
(*Act like you are looking at a jam-packed calendar with 0 availability*)
So I'm just looking at John's calendar here… Okk… hmm.. So John's calendar is really full…

Now, what I can do, because you're looking to work with us… is I can move a few things around for you… Would [X] or [Y] time work best for you? Then I'll be able to get you in directly with Lauren's business partner.
▸ BOOK THE TIME HERE WITH CLOSER.
Great — you mentioned earlier that you run decisions by [x], so what's their email address so I can invite them to the next call?
(Let them reply.)
Ok great. I am booking that now for you…. [3 seconds]
You should have received a confirmation email by now, did you get that? (Make sure they check.)

Ok great so now I'm sending you a document which breaks down our offer and how it works. It's really important you watch that, because when you speak with John he'll be able to break down, for YOU, how this system will work when applied specifically to your business.
John is really busy — so if you can't go through that before your call with him, can you let me know now? (Get confirmation they can watch it before.)
Ok great — when are you planning to watch it, so I can check in with you to make sure you've been able to go through it in full, and confirm your call with John?
Ok cool — I will hold you accountable to that. So expect a call or text from me right around then!
Just a note, your strategy session will take place on a google meet link, not a phone call. So please make sure you are somewhere quiet, where you can focus. Sounds ok?
It's been great chatting today — I'll be waiting for your reply to that email confirming you've been through the doc.
green_light: Strategy call booked + on the calendar
Confirmation email received + they checked
They committed to a specific time they'll watch the doc
They confirmed they can be on a google meet (not phone)
stages.pushback_script: They just gave you a soft commitment on watching the doc. Don't accept it. Push: 'John is really busy — so if you can't go through that before your call with him, can you let me know now?' Get a hard yes or move the call. A soft yes here = a no-show or unprepared prospect, which wastes John's time and burns the opportunity.

stages.name: 9b. Fit — Lauren Follow-up (not qualified)
stages.tone: Warm — they're not going to John, but Lauren will reach out personally.
stages.goal: Pass them to Lauren via DM follow-up. Confirm they're following her on the right platform and they'll be on phone to receive her message.
say: Cool. So with what you're looking to do, it's a pretty straightforward problem for us to solve.

Now, what I'm going to do for you is, I'll have a conversation with Lauren later today about everything we discussed here, and she'll personally reach out to you to send you the solution that's more aligned with what you're looking to do, which is [X, Y, Z].

I understand you are more active on [SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORM], so she'll be reaching out there, just to confirm and make sure you'll get her message — you know that sometimes it can land in the request folder, are you following her there?
(Let them reply — and make sure you check on your end in case they're lying about it.)

Okay perfect, could you send her a message now for me? I have a meeting with her right after this call so that way she can check your full profile and reach out to you in a few minutes, to make sure to cover all of your questions before getting you started.
Lauren checks her DMs a couple of times per day. What times later today could you be on your phone to have a chat with her?
green_light: Confirmed they follow Lauren on the right platform (you verified)
They sent Lauren a DM during the call
They named a time later today they'll be on their phone
stages.pushback_script: Make them do it NOW — don't let 'I'll do it later' slide. 'Cool — can you follow her right now while we're on, just so I know it's done?' Then verify on your end. People who say they'll do it later don't.

uncertainty_globals.description: Global uncertainty signals that always fire as a generic PUSH BACK alert, on top of stage-specific triggers.
uncertainty_globals.alert: Generic stall language. Don't move on. Push for specifics: 'Got it — but to be fair to your time, can you give me a clearer answer now so I can either get you to the right next step or save us both the time?' Then re-ask the question of the current section.

dm_workflow.goal: Book 3 QUALIFIED sales calls per day, of which 2/week become Accelerator members and 50% of the rest become Skool paying clients.

stages.name: 1. Opener
stages.tone: Light, fast, casual.
stages.goal: Hook them with a low-friction email ask + position you have multiple versions based on stage. Goal is to get their email + their stage in 2 messages.
say: MESSAGE 1: lemme get that to you. what is your best email address?
MESSAGE 2: and I have a few versions so can you tell me what stage of business you're at? 6 figures, 7+ figures, or just starting out — then I can send over the relevant one.
ADAPT — drop a quick personal line first based on their bio / what they commented. e.g. 'HipHopTV's vision is cool. Media companies are the way forward. Smart move…' then go into Message 2.
If you also connected on LinkedIn, slip in: 'Just accepted your connection request also :)'
green_light: You got their email
You got their stage of business
Logged in the CRM for follow-up (in case they ghost)
stages.pushback_script: Don't get pulled into explaining — keep them on the hook. Just say: 'It's a doc that breaks down exactly what we do based on your stage of business. So can you tell me — 6 figures, 7+ figures, or just starting out? Then I'll send you the one that fits.' Bring them back to the email + stage ask.

stages.name: 2. Get Stage (if email-only)
stages.tone: Friendly nudge.
stages.goal: If they only sent their email and didn't say their stage, loop back with one short line.
say: cool, and what is your stage? 😊
cool and what is your stage?
and I have a few versions so can you tell me what stage of business you're at? 6 figures, 7+ figures, or just starting out — then I can send over the relevant one.
green_light: You got their stage (just starting / pre-6 figs / 6 figs / mid 6 figs / 7+ figs)
Logged in CRM (Message 2 sent)
stages.pushback_script: Push gently: 'No worries — just throw out a rough monthly revenue or annual range, even if it's not exact. That way I can match you to the right version.' Get a number, not a vibe.

stages.name: 3a. Response — Starting out / 5 figs
stages.tone: Encouraging but direct.
stages.goal: Pivot from stage → their stuck point. Give them a list of options to anchor the reply.
say: ok cool, in that case I probably have a bunch of other stuff that could help you seeing as we've helped 100s and 100s of others start out successfully. what part of it are you the most stuck on? getting leads, getting yourself out there, sales, automations, or something else?
green_light: You know which part of their business they're stuck on
pushback_triggers: i don't know where to start
stages.pushback_script: Don't accept 'everything'. Pin one: 'I hear you — but if you HAD to pick the one that hurts the most right now, which would it be? Leads, sales, getting yourself out there, or automations?' One stuck point is enough to book.

stages.name: 3b. Response — not yet at 6 figs
stages.tone: Validate the gap between good + traction.
stages.goal: Anchor the goood-but-no-traction angle, then ask about their stuck point.
say: ok cool, in that case I probably have a bunch of other stuff that could help you seeing as we've helped 100s and 100s of others get over that hurdle of being GOOOD at what you do, but lacking the traction to hit 6 figs. what part of it are you the most stuck on? getting leads, getting yourself out there, sales, automations, or something else?
green_light: You know their specific traction gap (leads / visibility / sales / automations / other)
stages.pushback_script: Pin one: 'If you HAD to pick the single biggest thing keeping you from 6 figs, what would it be?' Then go from there.

stages.name: 3c. Response — 6 figs
stages.tone: Peer-to-peer, scale conversation.
stages.goal: Position the 6→7 figs angle, ask about their specific scale lever.
say: in that case I probably have a bunch of other stuff that could help you seeing as we've helped 100s and 100s of others start out successfully and scale from 6 to 7 figs. which part do you think you need support on to get from 6 to 7 figs so I can see what we got? client acquisition, automating more, or hiring?

MID 6 FIGS ADAPT: 'Given your business stage, plus the calibre of clientele you're working with, I probably have a bunch of other stuff that could help you. What are you currently looking to use LinkedIn for? Getting leads, sales, client retention, finding partners or something else? Then I can see what I may have which might serve you best.'
HITLIST RULE: any 6 figs+ prospect goes onto the 6-Figures+ Hitlist immediately, regardless of whether they reply. Goal = book a call. Cadence is in the Follow Up stage.
green_light: You know their 6→7 figs lever (acquisition / automation / hiring / other)
Added to the 6-Figures+ Hitlist
stages.pushback_script: If they're 6 figs and 'doing fine', flip it: 'Got it — so if you could magically fix ONE thing that would make scaling to 7 figs easier, what would it be?' Find the lever even if they downplay.

stages.name: 4. Get Problem → Book Call
stages.tone: Move quickly. Goal is the call.
stages.goal: Once they name their problem, book the call right away. If they ghost, send a voice memo.
say: oh, well we should find a time to chat for 5 or 10 mins this week. Which day would work?
we can see how we can help with that in a way that is a no brainer for you
green_light: Call time confirmed and on the calendar
OR if they ghosted: voice memo sent
stages.pushback_script: Don't let them push you into more info-dumping. Soft re-anchor: 'totally get it — 5 or 10 mins, just to see if we can help in a way that's a no-brainer for you. would [day] or [day] this week work?' Two specific options force a yes/no. If still ghosting → voice memo.

stages.name: 5. Send AI Training (casual)
stages.tone: Casual drop, no pitch.
stages.goal: Alternative track — drop the AI training link if the call isn't happening yet. Soft soft.
say: Lauren UTM: here's the link for the AI training: https://scalesystems.io/you-ai-start-org?utm_source=Facebook&utm_medium=DMs&utm_campaign=lauren
Mariana UTM: here's the link for the AI training: https://scalesystems.io/you-ai-start-org?utm_source=Facebook&utm_medium=DMs&utm_campaign=Mariana
green_light: Link sent with the right UTM (lauren / Mariana)
stages.pushback_script: No pushback here — casual drop, no commentary.

stages.name: 6. No-Reply Recovery
stages.tone: Light, no pressure.
stages.goal: Soft re-engage if they've gone silent. One short line.
say: If it's easier you can find a time here: [LINK]
green_light: Re-engagement message sent
stages.pushback_script: If they reply with stall language to this, jump into Follow-Up cadence.

stages.name: 7. Follow Up + Hitlist
stages.tone: Personal + genuine. No sales-y.
stages.goal: Two parallel cadences. NORMAL list: run the 3-touch weekly hitlist (voice memo -> value-add -> personal feedback). 6-FIGURES+ HITLIST: every 3rd day for 2 weeks with 1:1 value-add follow-up, then once per month indefinitely, PLUS a weekly broadcast email to the separate Hitlist email list. Goal of the hitlist = book a call.
say: NORMAL list — 3-touch weekly hitlist for prospects who DM'd but didn't convert:
Touch 1 — Voice memo: personal + casual, reference what they said before. Under 30 seconds.
Touch 2 — Value-add: a video that helps with their specific problem. No ask attached.
Touch 3 — Personal feedback: one piece of feedback specifically for them (like Lauren did with Pierre). Genuinely useful, not pitchy.
6-FIGURES+ HITLIST — separate, prioritised list. Goal = book a call.
1:1 cadence: send a value-add follow-up every 3rd day for the first 2 weeks, then once per month indefinitely until they book or ask to be removed.
Broadcast cadence: they also go on a SEPARATE weekly email list — one tailored email per week, specific to the hitlist (not the main newsletter).
Log every touch in the CRM. If they reply with a problem, book the call right away (jump to Get Problem -> Book Call).
green_light: NORMAL: Touch 1 (voice memo) sent
NORMAL: Touch 2 (value video) sent
NORMAL: Touch 3 (personal feedback) sent
6 FIGS+: scheduled into 1:1 every-3rd-day cadence (2 weeks)
6 FIGS+: added to weekly hitlist broadcast email list
All touches logged in CRM
stages.pushback_script: No pushback — these touches are value-only. If after all 3 they still don't engage, they go cold for now.

dm_workflow.style_rule: MIRROR THEIR STYLE every time. If they use capitalisation and proper grammar, you do too. If they use emojis, you do too. If they write lowercase + casual, match that. Match their energy, register, and length. Every DM is personalised to the prospect — the templates are a starting point, not a copy-paste.
dm_workflow.crm_rule: EVERY prospect you message gets logged in the CRM after Message 1 (so you remember to follow up if they ghost), and again after Message 2. If they're 6 figures or above, ALSO add them to the 6-Figures+ Hitlist (see Follow Up stage for the cadence).

outbound_workflow.goal: Dial leads who opted into our freebies (YOU-AI training etc.) within 24 hours. ONLY goal of the dial = book them onto the Scale Session triage call with Mariana. Do NOT try to qualify or pitch on the dial — the triage call does that. Verbatim source: Coach Cayden (Matt Ryder camp) — 'The Simple Way to Book More Calls (Outbound)' + 'Outbound Masterclass with Coach Cayden'.
outbound_workflow.style_rule: Tonality is EVERYTHING. Low-energy, conversational, almost clerical. Whoever wants something MORE loses the frame — be detached: 'I'll take a horse to water, drink it or don't, I have plenty of water.' Short sharp questions ('what got you looking into this?' / 'what do you mean?' / 'why's that?') — never long robot phrasing. BRIDGE every question to the next so it feels like a conversation, not an interrogation. Smile while you dial. When you hear their energy shift, CALL IT OUT — don't just keep going.

stages.name: 1. Pattern Interrupt + Disarm
stages.tone: Low-energy, conversational. Apologise BEFORE they push back — pre-empt the 'who is this' reflex. The word 'just' downgrades the stakes ('this is JUST Mariana').
stages.goal: Get past the first 5 seconds. Disarm them with an apology + the 'just' framing so they don't hang up. They opted into our freebie, that's the only hook you need.
say: Hey, is this [name]? … Yeah, I apologise, [name] — didn't mean to offend you or anything. I know I'm calling you out of the blue.
This is just [you] over here with Lauren Tickner's team — about the [YOU-AI training / freebie] you grabbed recently. Hopefully that rings a bell.

(If they say 'I don't remember'): Oh, I apologise — yeah, it's pretty common people don't remember. Looks like it was a couple of [days / weeks] ago. My job is just to get the information out to you — don't shoot the messenger. It'll take 5 minutes here, okay?
(Source: Cayden / Matt Ryder camp — Outbound Masterclass + Simple Way to Book More Calls)
green_light: They stayed on the line past the opening apology
They've acknowledged the opt-in (or accepted the 'don't shoot the messenger' frame)
stages.pushback_script: Stay calm, stay LOW energy. The 'don't shoot the messenger' line does the work: 'Yeah, totally fair — it's pretty common people don't remember. Looks like it was a few [days/weeks] ago. My job is just to get the information out to you, don't shoot the messenger. It'll take 5 minutes here, okay?' If they keep fighting (Cayden's gaslight-through principle): just repeat the same line in a different word order until they go with it. Most do.

stages.name: 2. Confirm 2 Pieces of Personal Data
stages.tone: Matter-of-fact, clerical — like you're a clinic receptionist.
stages.goal: This is the LOAD-BEARING move (Cayden's words: 'way harder to hang up' after this). Confirm 2 specific pieces of data they put on the opt-in form. After they say 'yes' to two of your questions, the hang-up reflex is gone.
say: Just needed to get a couple of things confirmed on our system here, if that's all right with you.
First thing here, it looks like I've got [piece 1 — e.g. their email / their stage of business / what they wrote in the form]. Is that correct?
Okay great — and I've got [piece 2 — e.g. their handle / their goal / their location]. Is that right?
(The exact data depends on what was on the opt-in form — but ALWAYS pick 2 things you can verify and ask about each one separately. Don't lump them.)
green_light: They've said 'yes' to TWO of your questions
stages.pushback_script: Keep it clerical: 'Totally fair — I'm just making sure I've got the right person matched to the right info on our end. Two quick things and we're done with that part — [piece 1], is that correct?' Then move to the surface question fast. Don't dwell.

stages.name: 3. Tipping-Point Question
stages.tone: Curious, no pressure — short sharp questions only.
stages.goal: Get ONE thing in their own words about why they grabbed the freebie. This is the dial's ENTIRE discovery — Cayden: 'I don't care about a problem. What I want to know is what they're looking for and why.' Don't go deep — the triage call does that.
say: Cool — so what got you looking into this in the first place? Or why did you want the [freebie] specifically? (Cayden's exact 'tipping point' question.)
(Variant): What caught your attention? What made you reach out in the first place?
(Variant for a specific freebie): I'm guessing you grabbed the YOU-AI training because you were looking to [insert obvious reason]? Or what were you hoping it would help with specifically?
(If they give a problem, great. If they give a goal, also great. Don't push for both — pick one and move on.)
green_light: You have ONE thing they want / one problem they're trying to fix
You DID NOT go deep into discovery — that's the triage call's job
stages.pushback_script: Push softly with curiosity (Cayden's bridging move): 'Got it — but if you had to point to ONE thing, what specifically caught your eye? Was it the AI angle, the revenue thing, something Lauren said?' Then move on — even a half-answer is enough to bridge to the booking. The dial is NOT the place to dig hard.

stages.name: 4. Book the Triage Call
stages.tone: Confident, light time-pressure. You're not asking permission — you're offering a fit-check.
stages.goal: Book the Scale Session (triage call with Mariana) NOW. Open loop on how we solve their thing — don't reveal the method. Cayden's exact mechanic: solvable + excited + time-pressure cover + cliffhanger.
say: The good news is — that's one of the easiest things for us to solve and help with. Honestly, when it's that kind of [thing], it actually makes me really excited for you, because it's usually fairly easy once I understand a bit more.

What I can do — I actually have a call I need to run to in a sec, I only had a second to reach out to you — but I have [time A] open this week, and [time B] open. Let's just schedule a quick chat with Mariana, who runs our Scale Sessions. What works best?
(Once they pick a time): Awesome. What's your best email so I can fire over the invite right now while we're on?
Quick note — it's a Google Meet, not a phone call. So make sure you're somewhere quiet, where you can focus. Sound good?

(THE OPEN LOOP / CLIFFHANGER): Mariana's the one who'll break down exactly how we'd do [the thing] for you specifically. I don't want to ramble through it now — she'll walk you through it properly on the call. Cool?
green_light: Time confirmed
Email confirmed + invite fired
Google Meet (not phone) confirmed
Open loop set — they DON'T have the full method, only a hook
stages.pushback_script:
FOR PRICE / COST QUESTIONS — Cayden's verbatim deflection: 'Well, there's a couple of different options. Why don't we do this — Mariana will walk you through the rest of how it works on the call, then she'll show you the options and we'll see which one makes the most sense, okay?'

FOR 'SEND ME MORE INFO' — don't send anything. The call IS the info. 'Totally get it — and to be straight, the Scale Session is just 15-20 minutes, no pitch. Mariana literally walks you through your situation and we see if it makes sense to keep talking. So [time A] or [time B]? Even a tentative slot — you can always move it.'

FOR 'LET ME CHECK MY CALENDAR' — flip to a soft tentative: 'No worries — let's pencil [time A] for now, tentative, and you can shift it if you need to. What's your best email so I can fire the invite over?'

FOR ANY HARD STALL — book a tentative + follow up: 'Cool, can I send you the AI training in the meantime and circle back in a couple of days?' Then onto follow-up (and Hitlist if 6 figs+).

stages.name: 5. Downplay + Show-Up Reinforcement
stages.tone: Casual, friendly, low-key. You're locking it in without making it feel locked.
stages.goal: Make them feel relaxed about the booked time (so they actually show up) + plant a 'I might call you before' anchor so a no-show feels rude. Cayden's exact moves.
say: Yeah it's no big deal — and hey, if I finish what I'm working on right before that, I might shoot you a quick message 15 minutes beforehand just to make sure you're set. Would that work?
Okay, and just give me a little bit of leeway the other direction too — if I'm running a couple of minutes late, no stress. Cool?
(Cayden: this gets you a SECOND yes after the booking — guilt-anchor for show-up. They've now said yes 2-3 times in a row, which makes ghosting feel rude.)
green_light: They said yes to the leeway / pre-call check
Calendar invite landed on their end (verify if possible)
stages.pushback_script: No pushback — this is closing flourish only. Move to wrap-up after.

stages.name: 6. Mid-Call Energy-Shift Recovery
stages.tone: Warm, curious, slightly puzzled — not accusatory.
stages.goal: If their energy dropped or you sense them clocking you as a sales call, address it directly. Cayden: 'When you hear that shift — call it out. Don't just keep going.'
say: Hey, I'm just curious and I apologise if I offended you or anything — I felt like we were having a really good conversation, and a second ago it feels like something shifted. What's going on?
(Then SHUT UP and let them answer. This often unlocks the real objection.)
(If they say 'I just realised this is a sales call'): Fair — and I get it. Honestly, this dial is just to see if it's even worth a deeper conversation. If it's not, that's totally fine — you tell me.
green_light: You've named the shift
They've responded with what's actually going on
stages.pushback_script: Not for this stage — this IS the recovery script.

stages.name: 7. Voicemail / No Answer
stages.tone: Quick + casual — like leaving a voice note to a friend. Under 20 seconds.
stages.goal: Drop a short voicemail that gets a callback. Then immediately follow up on the channel they opted in on (text or DM).
say: Hey [name], it's [you] from Lauren Tickner's team — just saw you grabbed the [freebie], wanted to ask you a quick question about what brought you there. Give me a quick text or call back at [number] when you've got 20 seconds. Cool, talk soon.
(Then immediately on text / DM): Hey [name] — just left you a quick voicemail re: the [freebie] you grabbed. Couple of seconds when you've got a sec? — [you]
(⚠ GAP — Cayden's videos don't explicitly cover voicemail. This is a sensible draft; refine once we find his voicemail teaching.)
green_light: Voicemail left (under 20 sec)
Follow-up text/DM sent on the channel they opted in on
Lead logged in CRM for retry
stages.pushback_script: No pushback for voicemails.

stages.name: 8. Outbound Follow-Up Cadence
stages.tone: Persistent without nagging. Value > volume.
stages.goal: Run the within-hour micro-cadence (Cayden's verbatim) FIRST, then a multi-day cadence. 6 figs+ goes onto the Hitlist after the multi-day cadence ends.
say: WITHIN-HOUR MICRO-CADENCE (Cayden/Matt, verbatim): For each lead, dial 3 times in a 1-hour block, spaced 20 minutes apart. ('1 hour, 3 calls — 20 / 20 / 20.') Track your pickup rate by hour in a separate calendar — green = 8%+, yellow = 5-8%, red = <5%. Dial during the green hours.
MULTI-DAY CADENCE (sensible default — flag for refinement from a future Cayden video):
Day 0 — dial + voicemail + text
Day 2 — re-dial different time. If no answer: short text 'still keen to chat re: the [freebie]?'
Day 4 — send the AI training link casually via text/DM (no ask)
Day 7 — final dial + voice memo: 'Hey [name] — couple of attempts, no pressure. If now's not the right time, totally fine — just let me know if you'd rather we circle back in a few weeks.'
IF 6 FIGURES+ → after Day 7, move them onto the 6-Figures+ Hitlist (every 3rd day for 2 weeks, then once monthly indefinitely, + the weekly hitlist email). Goal = book the triage call.
EVERY touch logged in CRM.
green_light: Within-hour 20/20/20 attempted on first dial day
Day 0 / 2 / 4 / 7 touches completed in order
All logged in CRM
If 6 figs+: moved onto Hitlist after Day 7
stages.pushback_script: Cadence runs regardless of replies. If they reply with a problem, jump straight to Tipping-Point Question -> Book the Triage Call.
